clue.text: Support poor foundation

blocks.note: first meaning: the part something stands or rests on
second meaning: an inferior grounding

explanation.walkthrough: The word serves as a noun for what holds something up and as an adjective meaning low or inferior, so the clue reads both senses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest supporting part of a structure is its footing, while as an adjective the word means mean, low or of little worth.

clue.text: Support includes piece slating those not here

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: backing is support, as for a cause
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A backer reinforces a structure by building another part into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The small piece goes inside the support after its first four letters, splitting it as BACK-BIT-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbiting is spiteful criticism of people behind their backs, when they are absent and cannot answer.

clue.text: Powerful performer on stage or in politics

definitions.note: the second sense borrows 'Powerful performer' from the first

blocks.note: first meaning: a circus or music-hall act who lifts great weights
second meaning: an autocratic leader who rules by force

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'Powerful performer', is read twice: once at the fairground and once in government.
explanation.definitionFit: The same compound names both a muscular entertainer lifting weights and a dictatorial ruler who governs through personal force.

clue.text: What old soldiers used for their investments?

definitions.text: What old soldiers used for their investments?

blocks.clueFragment: What old soldiers used for their investments?
blocks.note: surface reading: how retired servicemen placed their savings
setter's reading: to invest a town is to besiege it, so these are the trenches and ramparts built round it

explanation.surface: A question about where veterans put their pension money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' has an old military sense, to surround a fortified place; 'investments' therefore means sieges, not stocks and shares.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the earthworks, trenches and batteries an army throws up while blockading a besieged town or fortress.

clue.text: Elected to set contribution

blocks.note: a candidate who is elected is in
to put something is to set it down

explanation.surface: Someone newly voted in is about to make their mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone adds to a shared effort, such as ideas or work offered to a project.

clue.text: Divine old lady?

blocks.note: a god is a divine being
'old lady' is slang for one's mother

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like gushing praise; the whole clue doubles as the definition, a mother in God's name, with the question mark flagging the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother sponsors a child at baptism, a spiritual parent alongside the real one, hence a mother linked with God.

clue.text: General to dismiss protector when walking

blocks.note: the Duke of Wellington, the general who won at Waterloo
to boot someone out is to dismiss them

explanation.surface: A commanding officer is told to sack his bodyguard on the march.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellington boot, named after the duke, is a rubber boot (a welly) worn in mud and rain.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterproof rubber footwear keeps the feet and legs dry while tramping through wet fields or puddles.

clue.text: Hi-tech machine, British in origin

indicators.note: placed in means set within, so one word goes inside the other here

blocks.note: a root is an origin or source
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A boast that some piece of advanced machinery was invented in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British in origin' reads as a patriotic claim; it is an instruction to put B inside a word for origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated machine that carries out complex tasks, often programmed to replace human labour.

clue.text: Attractive divorcee in fringes of society

indicators.note: fringes are the edges, so only the end letters of the following word are used
placed in means set within, so the former spouse goes inside those edge letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of society
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: A glamorous divorced woman moves on the edges of high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy describes someone sexually appealing, which is one kind of being attractive or alluring.

clue.text: Personality under orders, not excitable

blocks.note: one's self is one's personality
someone acting under orders is controlled

explanation.surface: A description of a disciplined soldier who stays calm while obeying commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-controlled keeps their emotions in check and stays calm rather than getting worked up.

clue.text: Worry about opening of vicious cut

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the single letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that one letter is used

blocks.note: care is worry or anxiety
the first letter of vicious

explanation.surface: Fretting over how a nasty wound began.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, especially to slice meat or shape wood or stone with a blade.

clue.text: Oar and spar used on old steamer

blocks.note: a paddle is a short oar
to spar is to box, as boxers do in practice

explanation.surface: A list of a ship's wooden equipment: an oar and a mast-spar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' looks like a ship's pole beside the oar, but it is the verb meaning to box.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle-box is the casing over the large paddle wheel on the side of an old-fashioned paddle steamer.

clue.text: Savings group to do good for people generally

blocks.note: to benefit someone is to do them good
society is people in general

explanation.surface: A thrift club set up for the public good.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit society is a mutual association whose members pay in regularly to fund help in sickness or old age.

clue.text: Wooden quality of sets sold in jumble

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered heap, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A jumble sale offers wooden sets of furniture or toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' suggests a jumble sale, a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here it signals rearranging 'sets sold in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden manner means dull and expressionless, and stolidness is that impassive, unemotional lack of liveliness.

clue.text: High-spirited cat, like a young lad

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
boyish means like a boy

explanation.surface: A frisky kitten behaves like a little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomboyish describes a girl who is boisterous and lively in the rough-and-tumble manner expected of boys.

clue.text: Demanding tin is sent for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair gets taken apart and put back together differently

blocks.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists a dented tin be sent off to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' appears twice: once inside the fodder and once in 'tin is sent' as the definition's verb. The fodder is the three words 'tin is sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent keeps pressing their demands and will not accept refusal, so they are demanding.

clue.text: Crow kid left inside

indicators.note: inside says the abbreviation sits within the animal word, not beside it

blocks.note: a kid is a young goat
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A bird and a child are left indoors together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to boast; 'kid' looks like a child but is the goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow over a win is to boast about it, and to gloat is to show smug delight at success.

clue.text: Cavalier, about to depart, passed over

blocks.note: someone about to leave says they are off
to hand something over is to pass it

explanation.surface: A Royalist cavalryman, ready to ride away, is overlooked for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' suggests a Civil War Royalist, but it is the adjective meaning casually dismissive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is careless and dismissive, and offhanded behaviour shows the same casual lack of concern.

clue.text: Nobody has time for such a musical group

blocks.note: none means no one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A complaint that no one can find the time for a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine musicians, or a piece of music written for nine players.

clue.text: Miserable surf - or low waves

indicators.note: waves move to and fro, suggesting the letters toss about into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A surfer grumbles about poor conditions: the swell is either surf or low waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorrowful means feeling deep sadness or grief, which is a close match for being unhappy and wretched.

clue.text: For everyone like opposing chess players

blocks.note: first meaning: applying to all, without exception
second meaning: literally, facing each other over the chequered playing surface

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for 'applying to all' is read literally as where two chess opponents sit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means affecting all people or categories equally, as with a pay rise given to every worker.

clue.text: Lack of corn in tropic isle

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to remove
the Tropic of Capricorn, a line of latitude

explanation.surface: A shortage of maize on some island in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip CORN from the end of CAPRICORN, named in the Tropic of Capricorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a small island in the Bay of Naples, off the coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: Discover success has no return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a hit is a success
the word no written backwards

explanation.surface: Finding that a success brings no reward.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to come upon it by chance, which is to discover or find it.

clue.text: Smart piece of intrigue

indicators.note: a piece is a part of the whole, so the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: letters three to six of intrigue

explanation.surface: A clever bit of plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Trig is an old-fashioned adjective for neat and spruce in appearance, which is the dress sense of smart.

clue.text: It's distasteful to feel remorse about old measure

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remorse word goes round the measure

blocks.note: to repent is to feel remorse
the ell was an old unit of cloth length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: It is unpleasant to regret having to use some antiquated unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell sits inside after REP: REP-ELL-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent is disgusting and drives people away, so it is thoroughly distasteful and offensive.

clue.text: Greybeard with record that may be golden

blocks.note: first meaning: an old person
second meaning: an old popular song, as in the phrase 'golden' ...

explanation.surface: An old man holding a gold disc he once earned.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'golden oldie' is a hit song from years ago that is still popular.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is informal for an elderly person and also for an old song or film still loved.

clue.text: Works wearily to improve quality of sharpener

blocks.note: to grind is to toil at dull work
to tone is to firm up or improve the quality, as in toning muscles

explanation.surface: A craftsman toils tiredly to make a whetstone better.
explanation.definitionFit: A grindstone is a revolving stone disc used for honing knives and tools to a keen edge.

clue.text: Bridesmaid’s part in fixing date for Romans

indicators.note: a part found in the word means its letters are lifted from inside it

blocks.note: letters three to six of Bridesmaid's

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid's role in settling the wedding date.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides was the 15th of March, May, July and October and the 13th of other months.
